fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Terrain; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate the turn-in during nighttime or low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach both structures without obstruction.
• Maintain adequate width and overhead clearance along the access drive to allow a fire engine or ambulance to reach the detached structure.
• Post a simple site map near the driveway entrance showing the location of both structures, the parking area, and any utility shutoffs.
• Designate a specific area away from the driveway for visitor parking so the access drive remains open for emergency vehicles.
• Keep a gate or secondary path accessible at the far end of the driveway so vehicles can turn around without backing the full length of the drive.
• Identify and mark a secondary exit route across open terrain in case the single driveway becomes blocked during an emergency.
• Clearly number or label both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can immediately distinguish between them on arrival.
• Keep the area between the two structures open and passable so responders can move freely between them on foot or with equipment.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Long Driveway; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the structure on all sides.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between the canopy and the building.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation around the structure and along the driveway.
• Remove shrubs growing along the driveway edge that could block vehicle movement or spread fire toward the access route.
• Keep the single driveway clear of overhanging branches and low-growing shrubs along its full length.
• Maintain open gaps between shrub clusters so fire cannot travel continuously from one to the next toward the structure.
• Cut back ground vegetation in open terrain areas that connect directly to the structure.
